function: Learned downlink CSI compression and feedback with uplink-CSI assistance: disentangled-representation VAE network (DrCsiNet), encoder at UE, decoder at BS (p. 4)
system: FDD massive MIMO, 32-antenna BS, single-antenna UE, OFDM; Quadriga outdoor nLoS 3.59 GHz downlink, Dichasus indoor LoS 1.29 GHz downlink; no RIS (p. 9)
method: Disentangled-representation VAE: UE encoder for exclusive features, BS shared and virtual-shared encoders and recovery decoder; autoencoder-style end-to-end training with MSE and KL losses (p. 8)
data_channel: QuaDRiGa 3GPP UMa nLoS (3.59 GHz) and Dichasus indoor LoS (1.29 GHz) channels from a channel sounder [50]; 60,000 training samples each; 15,000 and 10,000 test samples (p. 9)
test_conditions: Separate train/validation/test sets for each channel model (Quadriga, Dichasus); sweeps over compression ratio 1/16-1/128, input-CSI noise and 8-bit quantization; no cross-channel test (p. 9)
baselines: Learned: CRNet, ACRNet-1x and 10x, DualNet, CRNet-U; non-learned: PCR codebook; ablations of DrCsiNet (pp. 9, 12)
metrics: NMSE and its CDF versus compression ratio (1/16-1/128), parameters, inference time, NMSE with 8-bit quantization and noisy input, per-user achievable rate with ZF (p. 9)
complexity: Parameters per module: DrCsiNet 133.288K at UE, 274.708K at BS (sigma=1/32, Table III); inference times plotted in Fig. 7 (p. 11)
q1_support: p. 9: "channel from [49], with the 3GPP uMA nLoS scenario"; [49] is 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 15).
q2_support: p. 12: "DrCsiNet exhibits strong generalization capabilities as it is not reliant on specific network structures" (other architectures, not new channels); p. 12: "we have introduced Gaussian noise various dB level to the input downlink CSI" (a CSI-error sweep); Table I (p. 9) gives separate train and test sets per channel model, with no cross-channel test.
q3_support: p. 9: "The NMSE of DrCsiNet is compared against the DL-based methods, including CRNet [23], CRNet-U [23], ACRNet-1x [24], and ACRNet-10x [24]"; p. 12: "the NMSE performance comparison with the PCR codebook [37], DualNet [38]" (PCR codebook as the non-learned baseline).
q4_support: p. 10: "We also assess the complexity of NN based on their parameters"; p. 11: Table III lists parameters at UE and BS (DrCsiNet 133.288K and 274.708K at sigma=1/32) and Fig. 7 plots the inference time.
q5_support: p. 9: "The second channel model uses the Dichasus channel from [50], using the indoor LoS scenario"; [50] is the DICHASUS channel-sounder dataset (p. 15). The paper gives no link to its own code.
notes: Include, area 2: DrCsiNet learns CSI compression and feedback with uplink-CSI assistance (p. 4). q1 rests on QuaDRiGa with the 3GPP UMa nLoS scenario ([49] is TR 38.901). q5 rests on the DICHASUS channel-sounder data [50], which the paper calls a 'channel' without saying 'measured' or 'public', so the reviewer should confirm it. q3: the PCR codebook [37] is taken as the non-learned baseline (a codebook design; p. 2 contrasts codebooks with DL methods), and the learned baselines are CRNet, ACRNet and DualNet; the reviewer should confirm that the PCR codebook is non-learned. q2 is 0: the 'generalization' is across network structures (p. 12), and each channel has its own split. Tables I-III and Figs. 6-14 were read from page images (pp. 9-13).
